title: Short-burst go-live simulation & KPI heatmap
content:
Purpose:
A compact, table-style KPI sandbox to run short-burst go-live simulations (0-72h) for betas and micro-launches. Meant to be used as a lightweight preflight and immediate post-launch triage tool — answers the question: "If traffic ramps to X qps for Y hours, which KPIs hit thresholds first and who fixes them?"

How to use: quick steps
1) Pick scenario from 'Sim Scenarios' (below).
2) Fill in expected qps/seq_len/avg_tokens and warm cache percentage.
3) Run simple sensitivity rules (bottom of sheet) or paste into the small python snippet in linked_artifacts.
4) Review KPI heatmap and assign owners for top-3 risks.
5) Record mitigation and follow-ups in the action log.

Core assumptions (editable):
- Model: rdx-open-7B / quant-4bit (hosted tier fallback to hosted-3B if saturating dedicated).
- Typical seq_len: 64 tokens (median), spike 512 tokens (worst).
- KV-cache warmup reduces per-token latency by 25% after prefix hits ~75% reuse.
- Autoscale cool-down: 300s, burst capacity unlimited for 15m but then queued.

Key metrics (columns in a sheet-friendly layout):
- Scenario name
- Owner (person)
- Start timestamp (UTC)
- Duration (h)
- Peak QPS
- Avg seq_len (tokens)
- Median latency p50 (ms)
- Tail latency p95 (ms)
- Error rate (%)
- Token cost / 1k tokens ($)
- Estimated GPU utilization (%)
- SLO breach risk (low/med/high)
- Primary mitigation (text)
- Status (open/monitor/closed)

Sim Scenarios (examples to copy into rows):
- short-burst-10k: 2h, peak 100 qps, seq_len 64, warm_cache 40% (use when marketing promo runs)
- overnight-stress: 8h, peak 350 qps, seq_len 128, warm_cache 20% (partner integration test)
- spawnstorm-15m: 0.25h, peak 800 qps, seq_len 32, warm_cache 5% (lambda cold wave)
- steady-growth-72h: 72h, peak 40 -> 200 qps, seq_len 64, warm_cache ramping to 80%

Quick interpretative rules (one-line formulas you can paste into the sheet):
- est_gpu_util = round(min(100, peak_qps * avg_tokens / 100000 * 100), 1)  # rough mapping tokens->GPU work
- est_token_cost = round((avg_tokens * peak_qps * duration_hours * 3600) / 1000 * token_price_per_k, 2)
- p95_exposure = if(warm_cache < 30%, p95 * 1.4, p95)  # naive warm-cache multiplier

KPI heatmap quick guide (coloring rules you can apply manually):
- Green: p95 < 350ms, error_rate < 0.2%, util < 70%
- Yellow: p95 350-700ms, error_rate 0.2-1.0%, util 70-85%
- Red: p95 > 700ms, error_rate > 1.0%, util > 85%

Top-3 predictable failure modes and playbook snippets:
1) Cold-KV storm (many prefixes cold)
   - Symptom: high p95 on first 5 minutes, then decays
   - Immediate mitigation: enable small warm-up run (10% traffic) and prefer cached variant; set fallback to hosted-3B for 15m window.
   - Owner: infra-eng oncall (Samir)
2) Token-cost runaway (unexpected long responses)
   - Symptom: token spend > 3x forecast
   - Mitigation: temporarily cap max_tokens at 128 (product toggle) and reduce temperature; pause non-critical batch jobs.
   - Owner: product-ops (Avery)
3) Autoscale lag -> queues and errors
   - Symptom: 502/504 spikes as scale lags
   - Mitigation: raise burst capacity and extend cooldown, enable canary fallback routing; notify SRE and roll back last model change.
   - Owner: SRE (Jordan)

Action log (example rows):
- [2025-01-13T03:12Z] short-burst-10k | observed p95 420ms | Mitigation: cap max_tokens -> set | Owner: Avery | Status: monitor
- [2025-01-13T03:46Z] short-burst-10k | hosted fallback engaged automatically | Owner: Samir | Status: closed

Acceptance criteria for go/no-go (simple checklist):
- p95 projected under load < 700ms for primary route OR automated fallback must maintain p95 < 1s with < 1% error.
- Token cost for first 24h within 150% of forecast.
- On-call contact assigned and reachable within 15m.
- Playbooks for the 3 predictable failure modes documented and linked.

Post-launch quick telemetry anchors (what to watch during first 3 hours):
- minute-by-minute: qps, p50, p95, error rate, autoscale events, fallback activations
- 5-minute aggregates: cost burn rate, model variant mix, median tokens per request
- Alerts to escalate: error_rate > 1% sustained 5m; p95 > 1s sustained 5m; GPU util > 95% sustained 2m

Notes & hypotheses to test in pilot:
- Hypothesis A: Prefilling KV-cache for top 10 routes reduces early-p95 by 30% — test in short-burst-10k by prefilling prefixes for 10% of traffic at t+0.
- Hypothesis B: Routing 20% of traffic to quant-variant reduces cost by 12% with <2% quality delta for low-risk endpoints.

Open questions (fill before signing off):
- What is the precise token_price_per_k for the reserved dedicated pool this sprint? (finance input)
- Are there outstanding model ABI changes scheduled inside the 72h window? (engineering)

Appendix: example small simulation snippet (psuedocode you can run locally)
- See linked_artifacts PR for runnable python. Simple logic: take scenario row -> compute est_gpu_util, est_token_cost -> compare to threshold -> mark SLO risk.

Footer: quick contacts
- Product Ops: Avery Chen (avery@redwood.ai)
- Infra SRE: Samir Patel (samir@redwood.ai)
- Oncall SRE: Jordan Brooks (pager: +1-555-214-1099)
- Engineering lead for serving-runtime: Lena Martinez (lena@redwood.ai)

This sheet is intentionally opinionated and pragmatic — copy rows into a live sheet during run, annotate changes in action log, and then convert the primary scenario to a reproducible test in the rollouts repo.
